tldr: WebArena is a realistic, reproducible web environment with fully functional sites across four domains and a benchmark of 812 long-horizon tasks, revealing that current LLMs achieve only 14.41% task success versus 78.24% for humans.
contributions: WebArena: a standalone, self-hostable web environment with fully functional websites from four domains (e-commerce, social forums, collaborative development, content management), enriched with tools and knowledge bases
A benchmark of 812 long-horizon, diverse web-based tasks with programmatic validators for evaluating functional correctness of task completions
Evaluation of baseline agents using LLMs (GPT-4, PALM-2), demonstrating a large performance gap between current models and human capabilities
methods: The authors built WebArena using open-source libraries to replicate real-world websites (OneStopShop, GitLab, Reddit, CMS) and imported sampled data from real-world counterparts. The environment includes utility tools (map, calculator, scratchpad) and knowledge resources (English Wikipedia, user manuals), all delivered as Docker containers with gym-APIs for reproducibility. They curated 241 task templates yielding 812 instantiated intents across three categories (information-seeking, site navigation, content/configuration operations). Evaluation uses programmatic validators (r_prog) for site navigation and content tasks, and three scoring functions (exact_match, must_include, fuzzy_match via GPT-4) for information-seeking tasks. Baseline agents were tested using few-shot in-context learning with GPT-4 and PALM-2.
results: The best GPT-4-based agent achieved an end-to-end task success rate of 14.41%, significantly lower than the human performance of 78.24%. The benchmark consists of 812 long-horizon tasks across e-commerce, social forums, collaborative development, and content management domains.
limitations: Current LLMs lack crucial capabilities such as active exploration and failure recovery needed for complex tasks. The best-performing agent achieves only 14.41% success, far below human performance of 78.24%, indicating that state-of-the-art LLMs are far from perfect performance on real-life web tasks.
